cards.front: What should you know about reasons for fitness testing?
cards.back: Identify strengths and weaknesses - find out which components of fitness need improvement Monitor progress - compare test results over time to see if training is working Set baseline scores - establish starting points for setting targets and designing training programmes Compare against normative data - see how results compare to national averages for age and gender Provide motivation - give performers targets to aim for and a sense of achievement Assess suitability for a sport - determine if fitness levels meet the demands of a specific activity

cards.front: What should you know about normative data?
cards.back: is a set of reference values (averages) that allow you to compare your test results against typical scores for your age and gender. Without normative data, a test score is just a number with no context.

cards.front: What should you know about pe exam tips — fitness testing?
cards.back: 1. For Fitness Testing questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Fitness Testing to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question

cards.front: What does Illinois Agility Run mean?
cards.back: Agility (e.g. Run through a course of cones set out in a 10m × 5m grid, including changes of direction, slalom sections and acceleration. Timed to the nearest 0.1 second.)

cards.front: What does Stork Stand Test mean?
cards.back: Balance (static) (e.g. Stand on one foot with the other foot placed against the supporting knee. Hands on hips. Time how long balance is maintained without the foot moving or hands leaving hips.)

cards.front: What does Multi-Stage Fitness Test (Beep Test) mean?
cards.back: Cardiovascular endurance (e.g. Run 20m shuttles in time with audio beeps that get progressively faster. Continue until unable to keep up with the beeps on two consecutive occasions. Score is the level and shuttle reached.)

cards.front: What does Wall Toss Test mean?
cards.back: Coordination (hand-eye) (e.g. Stand 2m from a wall. Throw a tennis ball against the wall with one hand and catch it with the other. Count the number of successful catches in 30 seconds.)

cards.front: What does Sit and Reach Test mean?
cards.back: Flexibility (hamstrings, lower back) (e.g. Sit on the floor with legs straight and feet flat against the sit-and-reach box. Reach forward as far as possible without bending the knees. Measure the distance reached in cm.)

cards.front: What does Sit-Up Bleep Test mean?
cards.back: Muscular endurance (abdominals) (e.g. Perform sit-ups in time with audio beeps that get progressively faster. Continue until unable to maintain the required pace. Score is the level reached.)

cards.front: What does Vertical Jump Test (Sargent Jump) mean?
cards.back: Power (leg) (e.g. Stand side-on to a wall and reach up with one hand (standing reach). Jump as high as possible and touch the wall at the highest point. Subtract standing reach from jump height. Measured in cm.)

cards.front: What does Ruler Drop Test mean?
cards.back: Reaction time (e.g. A partner holds a 30cm ruler vertically, with the 0cm mark between the thumb and forefinger of the person being tested. The ruler is released without warning. The distance the ruler falls before being caught is measured. Convert distance to time using the formula t = √(2d/g).)

cards.front: What does One Rep Max Test mean?
cards.back: Strength (e.g. Lift the heaviest weight possible for one complete repetition of an exercise (e.g. bench press, squat). The 1RM is the maximum weight that can be lifted once with correct technique.)
Speed (e.g. Sprint 30m from a standing start. Time the sprint using electronic timing gates for accuracy. Best of three attempts is recorded.)

cards.front: What does Handgrip Dynamometer Test mean?
cards.back: Strength (grip) (e.g. Squeeze a handgrip dynamometer as hard as possible. Record the score in kg. Best of three attempts for each hand is recorded.)
